classification\u003cbr>\u003cbr>During endoscopy, varices are carefully evaluated for characteristics associated with\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">hemorrhage risk, including size, tortuosity, red wale marks, cherry red spots, and active\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">bleeding. One commonly used endoscopic grading system is the Sarin classification, which\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">classifies esophageal varices according to their size and extent of luminal occupancy, helping\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">clinicians estimate bleeding risk, determine prognosis, and guide prophylactic or therapeutic\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">intervention.\u003c/p>\u003c/section>\u003csection class=\"page-group\">\u003cdiv class=\"page-label\">PAGE 25\u003c/div>\u003cfigure class=\"note-figure\">\u003cimg loading=\"lazy\" alt=\"Illustration associated with page 25\" src=\"data:image/webp;base64,
